key_insight: PRISM uses chemical priors as label-free learning signals to improve solubility prediction for unseen compounds, solvents, and solvent mixtures.
clinical_relevance: Better solubility prediction could support drug discovery, including oncology programs, but this study does not establish cancer-specific or clinical benefits.
method: Convert hydrophobic, electrostatic, polarizability, and substructural priors into relational teachers.
Pretrain four encoders by matching distance-based neighborhood distributions using KL divergence.
For mixed-solvent prediction, freeze the encoders and train a lightweight fusion-and-composition head.
evidence_signal: Across scaffold, solute, and solvent out-of-distribution evaluations, PRISM matched or surpassed baselines; mixed-solvent tests showed stronger performance and lower run-to-run variation, with ablations supporting the contribution of chemical relations.
watch_item: The abstract provides no dataset sizes or numerical effect estimates, limiting assessment of improvement magnitude and practical generalizability.
paper_title: PRISM: Prior Relational Information for Self-supervised Modeling to Enhance Solubility OOD Generalization
